" Hades was afraid, who reigneth over them that lie dead in the earth." Philo Byblius relateth out of Sanchoniathon (a more ancient writer than either Homer or Hesiod) not only that he was the son of Saturn and Rhea, but also that hisf father did canonize him after his death, and that the Phœnicians call him both Pluto and Muth, which answereth to the Hebrew מוּת, and in their language signifieth death. The Grecians, who had from the Phœnicians their first gods, as well as their first letters, tell us further, that this " Hadesg (or Pluto) was he who shewed men those things that did concern burials, and funeral rites, and honours of the dead, of whom no such care was had before his time: and that for this cause he was esteemed the god that bare rule over the dead; the dominion and care of them being assigned unto him by antiquity."
